items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I did not ever like Red Nichols or Bix Beiderbecke very much.

ctx.x: later you'd find little by little your own ideas would start coming in.

So when I first started to play I copied his solos note for note. And I would copy anybody's solos; but I did not ever like Red Nichols or Bix Beiderbecke very much. And when I went later years -- well, I'll get into that, it became kind of an issue. It was very racially divided in California, musicians were.
Do you recollect that old Italian teacher's name? Just for the record, who taught you to play French horn and --

items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: When I was a kid they had Louis Armstrong's book of 100 Hot Breaks, Red Nichol's 100 Hot Breaks and Whole Tone Scales

ctx.x: And you know, think of all the kids listening to this and saying, oh, that's heavy (humming). And that's all they do, a pentatonic scale and they've got these mathematical patterns. I've got books for those. They write books with all these patterns you can practice. And you can buy them anyplace. When I was a kid they had Louis Armstrong's book of 100 Hot Breaks, Red Nichol's 100 Hot Breaks and Whole Tone Scales, you can apply these anyplace. And we're right back to that. And they're stuck and nobody ever did it…
Now they've got their books of hot breaks, and memorizing these things. And laying them on top of you.
